statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH. Tail eases from 24 to 23 because the 28,992.25 session low has now held through a second hour and the index has stopped extending lower, while the 19:00 UTC power hour remains the single declared danger window. Tail stays below the block threshold.
recommendation: The cash Nasdaq-100 was 29,061.57 at 18:25 UTC, -395.40 points and -1.34% against a 29,456.97 previous close, inside an unchanged 28,992.25-29,267.42 session range. That is roughly 17 points below the 29,078.48 print at the previous assessment, so the hour produced sideways drift rather than a new low. The session low has stood since before 17:00 UTC and the earlier 275-point bounce off it is direct evidence that retracement is still being offered. Mapped policy state: WATCH, with a narrow 19:00-20:00 UTC danger window covering the closing hour.
headline: Nasdaq-100 steadies at 29,062 with the 28,992 session low intact as WTI tags a $90.13 day high, the 10-year prints 4.792% and VIX eases to 16.06
body:
The change this hour is an absence of continuation. At 17:26 UTC the index was 29,078.48, having just rejected the 29,267.42 bounce high; at 18:25 UTC it is 29,061.57. The 28,992.25 session low set earlier in the day has not been retested, and the session range is unchanged. Two consecutive hours of sideways drift in the lower third of the range, after a 275-point retracement off the low, is the opposite of the shallow-pullback, repeated-extension structure that defines a pathological path, so Tail eases one point to 23 rather than pressing toward the block threshold.

The cross-asset backdrop, by contrast, has firmed rather than decayed. WTI is $89.96, +4.90% on the day after tagging a $90.13 high, and Brent is above $94. The move follows verified U.S. military strikes on Iranian targets in the Strait of Hormuz, retaliation for overnight attacks on two oil tankers, which is a genuine geopolitical discontinuity rather than the continuation of a known conflict. The 10-year yield is 4.792%, sitting exactly at its day high, the 5-year is 4.550% and the 30-year is near 5.26%, close to multi-decade highs, within what is being reported as a worldwide government bond selloff. Long-end pressure plus an energy shock is a coherent valuation channel into Nasdaq-100 duration.

What keeps that from reading as one-way index structure is internal disagreement. VIX is 16.06, below its 16.15 session high and marginally lower than an hour ago, so the volatility bid is not accelerating alongside the new highs in crude and yields. Gold is down about 2.1%, which is inconsistent with a broad panic bid and more consistent with a rates-driven repricing. Megacap direction is split, with Apple and Meta higher while Microsoft, Amazon, Alphabet, Nvidia and Tesla are lower, and the semiconductor complex is weak but not uniformly so. That mixture raises Stress and holds Confidence high; on the standing calibration it does not by itself raise Tail.

Stress rises one point to 74, in the high band, reflecting crude and long-end yields both printing day highs and reported hawkish repricing of the September Fed meeting. Confidence holds at 88: live index, volatility, yield and crude levels were read directly from primary sources this hour, the Hormuz escalation and the bond-market move were verified in published reporting, and the seven-day U.S. calendar was checked against the economic calendar. The shared Finviz cross-asset context was 171 minutes old at assessment time, beyond the 90-minute freshness limit, so it was treated as stale and excluded from the price-path judgment.

The declared danger window remains 19:00-20:00 UTC. That is the U.S. closing hour, where auction mechanics meet an unresolved crude and rates shock, and where a loss of 28,992.25 is the specific condition that would convert the current range retest into a directional close. Outside that hour the mapped policy state stays at WATCH.

lookbackSummary: Twenty-three of the 24 preceding clock-hours carry a published Claude assessment; the 15:00 UTC hour on 1 September has none and is marked unavailable. The first fourteen slots, covering the 31 August U.S. session and the overnight hours into 1 September, all sat in the EA_ON band with Tail between 9 and 12 and mode mixed, while Stress drifted from 54 down to 50 and back up to 58 as crude firmed and long yields climbed. The regime broke at 08:00 UTC, when the Hormuz escalation and the associated crude move pushed Tail to 22 and mode to trend-down; Tail then held the 25-31 orange band from 09:00 to 13:00 UTC, peaking at 31 with Stress 75 around the U.S. cash open. From 14:00 UTC the picture improved as a genuine retracement developed: mode moved to event/whipsaw, Tail fell to 24 and then 21 at 16:00 UTC, before ticking back to 24 at 17:00 UTC when the 29,267.42 bounce high was rejected. The net shape of the day is a sharp event-driven repricing that has so far kept offering two-way trade rather than compounding into a one-way path.
outlookSummary: The projection starts from stabilisation rather than extension, so Tail opens at 23 for the current 18:00 UTC hour, two points under the block threshold. It lifts to 26 for the 19:00 UTC power hour, the single declared danger window, where closing-auction mechanics plus an unresolved crude and rates shock most plausibly convert a range retest into a directional close; a loss of 28,992.25 is the named condition. After the 20:00 UTC cash close Tail steps down to 22 and then into the teens, reaching an overnight floor of 12 across the mid-Asian hours, since post-close and Asian liquidity historically restore two-way rotation. The path lifts modestly through the European session on the global long-end selloff, then rises again on 2 September: 16 into the 12:15 UTC ADP release, and a second-day peak of 19 across the 13:30 UTC U.S. cash open and the following hour, which carries Factory Orders at 14:00 UTC and EIA crude inventories at 14:30 UTC directly into a live energy shock. Every one of those later readings is conditional risk, not observed structure. Confidence decays from 88 to 52 across the horizon, and Stress follows the same arc as Tail, staying in the elevated-to-high bands throughout because crude, the long end and the Hormuz situation are all unresolved.
